assumptions: The exact published ordinary 1911 Backgammon rules in RULES.md are carried over byte-identical and every preserved component keeps its function and quantity.
The two dice and the two cups are player-supplied under the inventor taste's allowance; this is packaging and changes no rule, probability or legal choice.

The 38 trough angles, trough floor radii and tip radii are carried over unchanged from the set being corrected, so tongue count, root widths, root join gaps, length spread and flame depth are arithmetically identical to it.
The tile bays and the trough clipping the previous correction introduced are withdrawn entirely: every tile ends on one exact circular arc at radius 89.85 and no tile plan is altered in any way.

Where a trough floor cuts inside radius 89.85 the outer corner of the tile lip above it laps up to 2.75 mm past the body ring; every such trough sits in the free window at a lane boundary, so the measured worst own-tile support under a counter stays 0.90769.
Geometric and print checks are required; no physical handling, print success, tile retention, stack stability, durability or dice fairness is claimed.

build_plan.exit_criteria: Sun body 191.1 x 192.5 x 9.0 with 24 blind lane pockets, a continuous rim ring at radius 84.5 and an unbroken flame crown of 38 tongues whose roots meet all the way round, each tongue tapering early, turning 25 to 45 degrees root tangent to tip tangent with at least 20 of that in its outer half, and carrying one plane-cut ramp from 8.0 mm at the root to a tip between 3.5 and 5.0 mm; one closed hero loop with the skirt running on underneath it; 24 separate lane tiles, twelve yellow and twelve cocoa brown strictly alternating, 2.8 mm thick on a 6.0 floor with tops at 8.8 and 0.15 mm clearance per side, every one ending on the same exact circular arc at radius 89.85; every entry passes the wall and overhang gates at a 0.4 mm nozzle.

Thirty counters at the unchanged 12 x 8 x 4 envelope with the original Bezier silhouettes, fifteen beige single-tail and fifteen dark-brown split-tail, each a single solid passing the wall and overhang gates at a 0.4 mm nozzle.

components.duty: Carries the 24 playable points in four banks of six, each with capacity 15 counters, plus the exposed capture bar. The corona ring is ornament: it carries no game state and receives no counter.
components.form: Disc 8.0 mm thick whose outer boundary is the flame crown itself rather than a circle: 38 tongues, every tongue touching both neighbours at the root so the crown is one continuous band of material. Each tongue is a swept blade, not an extruded triangle: it keeps the full width of its root chord, sheds that width early so its mid length is at most 0.441 of its root, and turns 29.74 to 39.60 degrees from root tangent to tip tangent with 21.95 to 29.23 degrees of that inside the outer half alone. Every tongue turns the same way round the ring. One plane per tongue then takes the top down from 8.0 mm at the root to a tip between 3.677 and 4.878 mm, 38 distinct heights, falling at 29.0 to 54.3 degrees, with crisp straight edges where the ramp meets each vertical flank. The thinnest tip measures 1.80 mm across in plan. Radial length runs from 2.325 to 9.085 mm and the narrowest root is 8.409 mm; the longest arc of plain circular edge left anywhere on the perimeter is 1.293 degrees, of which 0.000 degrees is tangential. 8 troughs cut to at least 9 mm of flame depth, the deepest 9.24 mm. One hero arch spans 18 degrees at the rim, rises to radius 99.0 and encloses one closed magnetic loop of 86.466 mm2 with two short tongues running on underneath it. Twenty-four shallow lane pockets radiate from a radius-24 centre platform whose broad planar top is 9.0 mm up.
components.interfaces: Twenty-four pockets, inner radius 26.35, outer wall at radius 84.5, floor 6.0, each with a 7.3 x 1.9 x 1.4 mm locating recess. Body between two pockets is 0.8 mm where exposed at 8.0 and 1.6 mm at the four bank boundaries, drafting 0.6 mm wider per side to the floor. The rim ring from radius 84.5 outward carries each tile lip at 7.8, and every tongue top holds 8.0 out to radius 90 before it starts to fall, so the ring stays full under that lip. Every trough that cuts inside radius 89.85 sits in the free window at a lane boundary, where no counter at the outermost station has any footprint.
components.name: Sun body
components.placement: Underside flat on the table at Z0. Deck top 8.0, pocket floors 6.0, rim ring top 7.8, centre bar top 9.0, four boundary capsule markers from 8.0 to 9.0. Every tongue is flat-bottomed at Z0 and its top falls from 8.0 to its own tip height, so nothing on the rim rises above the lane tops and nothing is cantilevered over air.

components.duty: Is playable point 1 and carries counters directly on its own top face. Its tone is lighter than the body, so lane identity is a real part in its own filament rather than paint or texture.
components.form: Annular-sector strip on lane axis -75.0 degrees, inner radius 26.5, outer edge one exact circular arc of radius 89.85 centred on the board, 2.8 mm thick with a flat broad coplanar top and exposed top edges rounded 0.15 mm. The outer 5.5 mm thins to a 1.0 mm lip. All 24 tiles carry that same arc, so the fan closes on one continuous circle: no notch, no scallop, no bay and no shortening is cut into any tile end, and no orange flame root is visible inside that circle.
components.interfaces: 0.15 mm plan clearance per side at the pocket opening, matching the pocket's 0.6 mm per side draft. One radial stadium key 7.0 x 1.6 x 1.2 mm on the underside, centred at radius 78.5 and offset 7.0 mm from the lane axis, 2.05 mm clear of every counter landing region.
components.name: Lane tile, point 1
components.placement: Seated on the pocket floor at Z6.0 so the top lands at Z8.8, standing 0.8 mm proud of the body, with its lip lapping the rim ring at Z7.8.

concept.interaction: Two players each own 15 single-tail or split-tail counters and each supply one ordinary six-sided die cup; the pair shares two ordinary 1-6 dice of any standard make, which the set does not include. They move opposite ways around the Sun across 24 lane tiles in four banks of six, hit single opposing counters onto the exposed circular centre bar of the sun body, enter barred counters before any other move, and drain all 15 beside their own six-point home bank to win. Every component keeps its ordinary 1911 Backgammon function. The legal signature 6,2 roll shows its six-point first submove: one attacker replaces a lone split-tail counter at the near rim and the victim lifts 80 mm to the low centre bar. Historical opening choices, whole-throw use, doubles, touch laws, 1/2/3 results and series starts remain binding as RULES.md states them.
concept.print_stance: All 55 components print flat-bottomed. The Sun body prints underside down; every tongue has material removed from its top only, so no face overhangs and the overhang gate reports zero regions needing support and zero bridges. Each lane tile prints top face down so its locating key points up; each counter prints on its flat bottom. Nozzle 0.4 mm on a 200 x 200 x 200 mm bed.
risks: A counter at the outermost 85 mm station overhangs its tile: 0.90769 of the footprint lands on its own tile, the rest passes the radius-89.85 tile edge, and that overhang is reported rather than hidden.
Tiles are gravity-seated with one locating key; retention force is not tested and is not claimed.

The tile lip laps up to 2.75 mm past the body ring at the deepest troughs. Each tile prints flat and alone, so that tab costs no printed overhang and no support, but it is an unsupported corner in the assembled board and no handling test has been run on it.

The flame crown is short by design. The reference proportion needs a 210 to 230 mm envelope and will not fit the declared 200 mm bed, so length stays capped at 9.085 mm and the crown earns its read from taper, curl and the falling top instead.
concept.signature_decision: The signature is the flame crown reshaped into blades. Each of the 38 tongues keeps the full width of the root it shares with both neighbours, sheds that width early so its outer half is slender, turns 29.74 to 39.60 degrees from root tangent to tip tangent with 21.95 to 29.23 of that inside the outer half alone, and lies back: one plane takes its top from the deck height at the root down to a tip between 3.677 and 4.878 mm, with crisp edges where that ramp meets each vertical flank. The 24 lane tiles end on one exact circular arc at radius 89.85, so the flame lives entirely outside a clean circle and the board reads as one whole object.
concept.summary: Backgammon - coronal-rain theme: rival streams of condensed plasma travel magnetic lanes, scatter lone drops, and rain back into a Sun whose fan of lane tiles closes on one clean circle and whose rim is a crown of curled flame laid back off that circle.
concept.title: Rainward Bladefire

astronomy_sources.claim: Cooling plasma follows magnetic structures and can switch paths through reconnection. This supports the coronal-rain subject and the closed magnetic loop in the corona rim; it supports none of the game's blocking, probability or result mechanics.

baseline.note: RULES.md is carried into this revision byte-identical. Historical instructions, reviews, reports and publication records in the clone are reference data, never current authority or passing evidence. The original publication is not updated; this revision takes a fresh finalization and a normal Release.

closest_collisions.difference: Lunar phases applied to a conventional luxury board. Rainward Corona uses radial plasma lanes as separate two-tone tiles and a corona rim of irregular prominences.
A circular backgammon board already exists, so the circle is not claimed as novel. No file, dimension, geometry or artwork from it is used.

research.current_access: Correction-only reuse of the frozen published research and rules from the cloned set; the original source access dates are retained as historical evidence, not newly verified web claims. The immutable revision-source.zip baseline, the local clone's CAD, its archived renders and RULES.md were inspected on 2026-09-18 before any geometry was written.

design_changes.current: Each tongue is a swept blade: full root width, width shed early so mid length is at most 0.441 of the root, a 29.74 to 39.60 degree turn from root tangent to tip tangent with 21.95 to 29.23 degrees of it inside the outer half, and a single plane-cut ramp from 8.0 mm at the root to a tip between 3.677 and 4.878 mm.
design_changes.previous: Each tongue was a broad flat triangle extruded at the full 8 mm deck height, with a vertical wall all the way round and only a small hooked nub at the apex.
design_changes.reason: The correction Wish. A solid block at any angle other than straight down made the rim read as a cog or the crimped edge of a bottle cap rather than as fire coming off a sun.

design_changes.current: Material comes off the top only, cut by one plane per tongue, so both flank edges stay crisp the whole way out and every underside stays flat on the bed.
design_changes.previous: Material was taken off the top and the flanks together in an earlier attempt, blending the top surface into the flanks.
design_changes.reason: The correction Wish names that earlier attempt: blended tops made the tongues look like drips of melted wax slumped over the edge. A downward taper would also cantilever over air and need support.

design_changes.current: Every tile ends on one exact circular arc of radius 89.85 and no tile plan is altered in any other way; the flame lives entirely outside that arc.
design_changes.previous: Every tile end was bayed at the lane boundaries and clipped back into any trough that cut inside radius 90, so the fan of 24 tiles did not finish on a circle.
design_changes.reason: The correction Wish abandons the orange-flame-root idea outright. The bays made every tile look bitten and the board stopped reading as one piece.

design_changes.current: Each tile and pocket is two lines and two exact arcs, and each flank is a short chain of cubic Beziers fitted to within 0.045 mm; the Sun part is 5.6 MB and the assembled export 7.9 MB.
design_changes.previous: Tiles and pockets were sampled as 28 to 180 chord polygons and the flanks as dense Bezier chains, which made the Sun part 11.7 MB and the assembled export 48.3 MB.
design_changes.reason: The correction Wish caps the exported geometry. The Sun part misses its 4 MB target because the preserved 280-sample hero arch plan cannot be touched.

research.inventor_method: Mara Masque's taste is applied directly by the root Manager: this runtime materialises no mara-masque custom subagent, so no Inventor delegation was fabricated. The independent blind review of the canonical images was delegated to a separate native critic that had not seen the Wish.
